title: Senior Noncommissioned Logistician
raw_text:
10-92Z. MOS 92Z--Senior Noncommissioned Logistician, CMF 92 (Effective 202610)
    a. Major duties. The senior noncommissioned logistician supervises Soldiers engaged in supply and
services, materiel, petroleum, fatality and culinary management, aerial delivery operations, shower and
laundry, water treatment and logistics operations. They performed these duties in a multifunctional
logistics environment and the senior noncommissioned logistician must be qualified in one of the following
seven MOS (92A, 92Y, 92F, 92G, 92M, 92R, and 92S) at the grade SFC. Duties for MOS 92Z at each
level of skill are:
        (1) MOSC 92Z5O. The Senior noncommissioned logistician Master Sergeant (MSG) supervises
duties in preceding skill levels and supervises operations of organizations performing supply and logistics
related service operations such as decontamination, transportation, and property disposal operations.
They supervise the planning of all classes of supply requirements in support of Army operations based on
the operational environment. Supervises open and covered storage, receiving, classification, issue
materiel handling, supply locator systems, facility safety and supply security operations. Supervise
management of materiel support functions in stock control and accounting, procurement, inventory control
and item financial management. Supervises development and preparation of operations information,
plans, maps, sketches, overlays and related data to employment supply and service organizations.
Analyzes reports on supply and service support operations. Performs duties as petroleum quality
assurance representative. Assists command and staff officers in appraisals of petroleum and water
operations. Develop, coordinate, implement, advise, and evaluate command food service programs.
Monitor requests for food items and equipment. Develop and analyze menus and coordinates menu
substitutions. Evaluate operation of garrison and field kitchens, food service training facilities and
maintenance of equipment. Survey individual preferences, food preparation and food conservation.
Prepare reports, studies, and briefings on food service operations. Supervises fatality management
activities, provides technical and administrative support on graves registration matters, acquisition of land
for temporary cemeteries, equipment requirements for mortuaries, and recovery/evacuation procedures.
Supervises operations of organizations performing airborne and resupply by airdrop missions. Supervises
development and preparation of operations information, plans, maps, sketches, overlays, and related
data to facilitate airborne operations. Advises on airborne operational matters and performs liaison
between staff and supported personnel. Performs duties as quality assurance representative for all
shower/laundry and clothing repair functions. Provides technical guidance to junior grade personnel.
Develops countermeasure policies, plan, doctrine, and operating procedures. Supervises development
and preparation of operations, information, plans, maps, sketches, overlays, and related data to employ
all logistical (supply & service organizations) in Army, Joint, Interagency, Intergovernmental, and multi-
national operational forces in support of worldwide land and contingency operations. Contributes to
subordinate and staff development and operations of the GCSS-Army automated system, equipment
review, salvage, demilitarization, and unit/organizational and repair parts supply procedures within the
operational area. Perform liaison between joint and allied staff and supported personnel to improve
effectiveness of all support activities.
        (2) MOSC 92Z6O. The senior noncommissioned logistician Sergeant Major (SGM) serves as the
principal NCO of logistics support operations and performs supervisory duties shown in preceding level of
skills. They provide technical guidance to subordinate personnel and advise senior leaders on logistical
operations. They are the senior enlisted advisor to Commanders, Directors, and Chiefs of Departments
and staff agencies on all matters pertaining to enlisted personnel. The senior noncommissioned
logistician Sergeant Major (SGM) must be knowledgeable in all operations of organizations performing
logistics related service operations. Must be able to plan, coordinate and supervise activities pertaining to
unit organization, training, tactical and technical operations. Success in this MOS requires demonstrated
expertise in a variety of progressive assignments including leadership, key billet, and staff positions at the
strategic, operational, and tactical levels.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Senior noncommissioned
logisticians, MOS 92Z, must possess the following qualifications:
         (1) Physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
         (2) Physical profile of 222232.
         (3) Minimum score in aptitude area – not applicable.
         (4) A minimum OPAT score – not applicable
         (5) No aversion to the sight of handling of needles, human tissues, blood, skeletal and/or
decomposed human remains.
         (6) Qualification scores – not applicable.
        (7) Must possess finger dexterity in both hands.
        (8) Per AR 600-8-19, promotion to MSG and SGM requires an interim secret eligibility or higher.
   c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
MOS).
        2S – Battle Staff Operations NCO.
        3C – Operation Contract Support Course (OCSC) (SSG thru SGM).
        8R – Master Resilience Trainer (MRT).
        3D – Level II Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) Industrial/Contract
Property Management Certification.
        D6 — Operational Data Analyst (personnel only).
   d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
        (1) Table 10-92Z-1. Physical requirements.
        (2) Table 10-92Z-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (3) Table 10-92Z-3. Standards of grade TDA.

The senior noncommissioned logistician supervises Soldiers engaged in supply and services, materiel, petroleum, fatality and culinary management, aerial delivery operations, shower and laundry, water treatment and logistics operations.
Manage activities related to strategic or tactical purchasing, material requirements planning, controlling inventory, warehousing, or receiving.
They supervise the planning of all classes of supply requirements in support of Army operations based on the operational environment.
Supervise the activities of workers engaged in receiving, storing, testing, and shipping products or materials.
Supervises open and covered storage, receiving, classification, issue materiel handling, supply locator systems, facility safety and supply security operations.
Perform both supervisory and management functions, such as accounting, marketing, and personnel work.
Supervise management of materiel support functions in stock control and accounting, procurement, inventory control and item financial management.
Supervise and provide instructions for workers collecting and tabulating data.
Supervises development and preparation of operations information, plans, maps, sketches, overlays and related data to employment supply and service organizations.
Prepare operational or risk reports for management analysis.
Analyzes reports on supply and service support operations.
Serve as a technical liaison between quality control and other departments, vendors, or contractors.
Performs duties as petroleum quality assurance representative.
Represent organization at personnel-related hearings and investigations.
Assists command and staff officers in appraisals of petroleum and water operations.

Advise food service managers and organizations on sanitation, safety procedures, menu development, budgeting, and planning to assist with establishment, operation, and evaluation of food service facilities and nutrition programs.
Develop, coordinate, implement, advise, and evaluate command food service programs.
Monitor use of government food commodities to ensure that proper procedures are followed.
Monitor requests for food items and equipment.
Analyze menus or recipes, standardize recipes, or test new products.
Develop and analyze menus and coordinates menu substitutions.
Direct the operation and organization of kitchens and all food-related activities, including the presentation and serving of food.
Evaluate operation of garrison and field kitchens, food service training facilities and maintenance of equipment.
Observe clients' food selections and recommend alternate economical and nutritional food choices.
Survey individual preferences, food preparation and food conservation.

Advise food service managers and organizations on sanitation, safety procedures, menu development, budgeting, and planning to assist with establishment, operation, and evaluation of food service facilities and nutrition programs.
Prepare reports, studies, and briefings on food service operations.
Supervise funeral processions and assist with cemetery parking.

Supervises fatality management activities, provides technical and administrative support on graves registration matters, acquisition of land for temporary cemeteries, equipment requirements for mortuaries, and recovery/evacuation procedures.
Coordinate flight activities with ground crews and air traffic control and inform crew members of flight and test procedures.
Supervises operations of organizations performing airborne and resupply by airdrop missions.
Procure, produce, and provide information on the safe operation of aircraft, such as flight planning publications, operations publications, charts and maps, or weather information.
Supervises development and preparation of operations information, plans, maps, sketches, overlays, and related data to facilitate airborne operations.
Coordinate with agencies, such as air traffic control, civil engineers, or command posts, to ensure support of airfield management activities.
Advises on airborne operational matters and performs liaison between staff and supported personnel.
Provide or arrange for services such as clothes pressing, cleaning, or repair.
Performs duties as quality assurance representative for all shower/laundry and clothing repair functions.
Provide technical support to junior staff or clients.
Provides technical guidance to junior grade personnel.
Develop and document security procedures, policies, or standards.
Develops countermeasure policies, plan, doctrine, and operating procedures.
Perform general personnel functions, such as supervision, training, and scheduling.

Supervises development and preparation of operations, information, plans, maps, sketches, overlays, and related data to employ all logistical (supply & service organizations) in Army, Joint, Interagency, Intergovernmental, and multi- national operational forces in support of worldwide land and contingency operations.
Direct the analysis, development, and operation of complete computer systems.

Contributes to subordinate and staff development and operations of the GCSS-Army automated system, equipment review, salvage, demilitarization, and unit/organizational and repair parts supply procedures within the operational area.
Direct, supervise, assess, and communicate with supportive personnel.
Perform liaison between joint and allied staff and supported personnel to improve effectiveness of all support activities.
Supervise or advise subordinate personnel.
They provide technical guidance to subordinate personnel and advise senior leaders on logistical operations.
Supervise or advise subordinate personnel.
They are the senior enlisted advisor to Commanders, Directors, and Chiefs of Departments and staff agencies on all matters pertaining to enlisted personnel.
Perform general personnel functions, such as supervision, training, and scheduling.
Must be able to plan, coordinate and supervise activities pertaining to unit organization, training, tactical and technical operations.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
